detail:
fnn-owner-limit-serialized (admin.lisp:534) deliberately observes the history off the mutex (comment at admin.lisp:~545, sweep S033). The deciding quantum runs under O (fnn-quantum-control, admin.lisp:~560) and E (fnn-with-observed-mutex *fnn-extent-lock*, admin.lisp:~565), and at admin.lisp:~578 takes `(if (equal values seen) history (fnn-heap-history-observation (fnn-store-root store) values))'. When a concurrent limit change moved the carry between the off-mutex read and the deciding quantum, the else branch runs under O and E: fnn-heap-history-observation (heap.lisp:255-256) -> fnn-heap-history-octets / fnn-heap-log-records (heap.lisp:272) -> fnn-heap-directory-octets (heap.lisp:244) -> fnn-lstat (io.lisp:612) and fnn-list-directory-bounded (io.lisp:835 opendir, 838 readdir, 847 closedir), plus one fnn-lstat per directory entry (heap.lisp:~246).
Keys: R2|fnn-list-directory-bounded|E:sb-posix:opendir, ...|E:sb-posix:readdir, ...|E:sb-posix:closedir (E sites 2), and the E site of R2|fnn-lstat|E:sb-posix:lstat (admin.lisp:578 chain; the same key is also reached by LOCK-R2-LIVE-RECONFIGURE-IO). The listing is bounded (fnn-heap-listing-bound) but is per-segment lstat I/O.
Reachability: only on a race of two concurrent `store limit' requests (the branch is the documented re-observe path); the loop at admin.lisp:~549 exists precisely to make it rare. The path is live code, not dead: it is the fallback of the S033 design.
fix: Make the deciding quantum refuse-and-retry (return to the observation loop, off the mutexes) instead of observing under them when the carry moved; the ACL2 decision then runs only on a history observed over the carried profile. If instead kept, declare it as an exception citing the race-only reachability.
notes: Fixed: deciding quantum returns :carry-moved and the loop re-observes off O/E; fnn-lim-decision history now required. Removed opendir/readdir/closedir E keys; lstat E remains (live-reconfigure chain). natives_owed: tests/test_native_limits_live.py, tests/test_native_public_limits.py (concurrent store limit), tests/test_native_admin.py.

lock-io-out statement: O/E exclude the limit decision; history directory I/O already runs off both locks. The carried profile and history are staged, and the deciding quantum rechecks the current carry, returning :carry-moved to reobserve off-lock on mismatch. No limit mutation happens on that retry branch. Verified current tree; live-reconfigure I/O remains the other lane’s item.
lock-io-out natives owed for the existing fix: tests/test_native_limits_live.py and tests/test_native_public_limits.py.
scenario: Two operators change the limit concurrently; the loser's deciding quantum finds values != seen and walks the journal directory while holding O and E.
